oneLine: Solid lemmas, sentence translations and an excellent chat partner, but it gets dáselo's grammar wrong and its drill and phrase cards are full of broken blanks and ser/estar errors.

mistakes.what: grammarNote is false: "In Latin America, 'tú' commands use '-s' ending (e.g., 'dáselo'). In Spain, it would be 'dáselo' (same) or 'dale'". There is no -s command ending. The s belongs to the clitic se (dá + se + lo).
formation repeats the error: "ending '-s' (tú) + clitics 'lo' ... + 'se'". It also has filler ("vowel change 'a' to 'a' (no change)") and labels the tense "present" with mood imperative.
It never explains that se stands in for le before lo (le lo → se lo), which is the key point of this form.
The clitics list only has se ("accidental se"). The indirect object me (the person who forgot) is missing, so the learner can't see why the 3rd-person verb means "I forgot".
grammarNote is filler and misleading: it calls this "a common Latin American construction" and then says Spain uses "'se me olvidó' as well".
grammarNote: "'Ser' is used for permanent or temporary states". Temporary states take estar, so this teaches the ser/estar split wrongly. Events (la fiesta) are the right reason here.
It doesn't mention that in Latin America extrañar is the everyday verb for "to miss" and echar de menos sounds Spanish or bookish. The roots are also off: echar comes from Latin iactare, not iacere.
roots say "From Latin 'ire'", but fui comes from Latin fui (the perfect of esse). Only the infinitive ir comes from ire.
roots list the non-word "comestics" as an English cognate.
roots "From Latin 'sed non'" is wrong. Sino is si + no.
roots call English 'cage' a cognate of caja (cage comes from cavea and caja from capsa).
roots say "From Italian 'banco'". Spanish banco is Germanic in origin; only the financial sense passed through Italian. "desk (in a classroom)" is a stretch (that is pupitre).
It doesn't explain that 'me quedé' is pronominal quedarse (to stay) and gives no clitic entry for me. The note "to arrange to meet" is mainly Spain usage (quedar con alguien).
It is not flagged as the idiom 'dar pena' (isIdiomOrPhrase missing). It also doesn't say that this 'embarrassed' sense is Mexican, versus 'it makes me sad' elsewhere.

mistakes.item: Hace dos años que vivo aquí.
mistakes.what: The translation is right, but the phrases list is empty. It misses the hace…que time construction.

mistakes.item: Sin embargo, no se dio cuenta de nada.
mistakes.what: The translation adds "at all". It is a small embellishment.
Being shy as a child is a character trait and needs ser: "eras muy tímido". The English "used to be very shy" also points to ser. The card teaches a wrong ser/estar choice.

mistakes.item: Nosotros ___ tarde para la película. (vamos a estar)
mistakes.what: "estar tarde" is ungrammatical for being late. Spanish says llegar tarde (vamos a llegar tarde).

mistakes.item: Espero que yo ___ listo para el examen. (esté)
mistakes.what: With the same subject Spanish needs the infinitive: "Espero estar listo". "Espero que yo esté" is unnatural.

mistakes.item: Nosotros ___ muy cansados después del trabajo.
mistakes.what: The English says "always tired" but the Spanish has "muy" and no siempre. The two don't match.

mistakes.item: Yo ___ en la fiesta ayer. / Tú ___ enfermo la semana pasada.
mistakes.what: "I was at the party" and "You were sick last week" don't force the preterite; estaba/estabas fit just as well. That's harsh for a one-try drill.
"¿Cuáles de estos libros es tuyo?" is ungrammatical with the singular verb. It should be Cuál.
The English is "What time does the pharmacy close?" but the answer is "Qué". "¿Qué cierra la farmacia?" means "What does the pharmacy close?". It needs A qué hora.

mistakes.item: Llegamos al aeropuerto a las cinco de la tarde ___. (ayer)
mistakes.what: On a verb card for llegar the blank is the adverb "ayer" and the verb is already written out, so the card drills nothing.

mistakes.item: Yo pagué la cuenta en el restaurante ___ pasado. (anoche)
mistakes.what: The answer isn't the verb pagar, and "anoche pasado" is nonsense, so it doesn't fit the blank.

mistakes.item: Ellos ___ muy felices con el regalo. (van a ser)
mistakes.what: A reaction to a gift is a state and needs estar: "van a estar muy felices/contentos". "van a ser" teaches the wrong verb.
Before a noun the standard form is "¿Qué días trabajas?". "Cuáles días" is colloquial and shouldn't be the taught answer.
The note says azúcar is simply feminine, but it is mostly used as masculine (el azúcar) in Mexico, so learners will be confused.

mistakes.item: ___ la primera pastilla en la mañana. (Toma)
mistakes.what: The English has "!" but the Spanish has no ¡…!. The note "use the present tense form of the verb (tú form)" is misleading: the tú present is tomas, and the command matches the él form.
The English "Why are you late?" is present tense but the Spanish is preterite (llegaste).
The sentence is stilted in both languages (more natural: "Te voy a creer").
The "(formal)" in the English is odd and serves no purpose.
"Los sándwiches siempre quedan ricos en la playa" is slightly odd; "saben más ricos" would be more natural.

strengths: All tricky lemmas are right: fui=ir, fue=ser, vino=noun wine, como=comer, plus the gerund with an enclitic in observándome.
It catches the me da pena = embarrassed and llevar + time duration readings.
Sentence translations are accurate, it spots sin embargo, darse cuenta, a lo mejor and echar de menos, and it invents no idioms in 'El perro come pan'.
Phrase cards use Mexican vocabulary (camión, ahorita, en la mañana) and nothing Spain-only.
The chat replies are short, natural and Mexican (¡Qué padre!) and keep the conversation going.
All four corrections are right: a la playa + comimos, la comida fue muy buena, and both correct sentences are left alone (Yo kept).
